contradictions.detail: Seller's opening comment says 'only 89k miles' while the listing body and Essentials state 90k miles; consistent with rounding rather than a real conflict, but the exact odometer reading should be confirmed on the dash photo/PPI.

critical_evidence.evidence: Listing states timing belt and water pump were replaced in March 2026 at approximately 86,000 miles, and the seller names Willard's Auto Repair in San Jose as holding the record. The Carfax snapshot shows 5 service records but the specific dated invoice is not reproduced in the listing text examined here.

Sport Package KDSS plus factory rear height-control air suspension. Photos show a level, correct stance with no sag and no lift or aftermarket components. The seller posted a dedicated air-suspension video, which was not examined here; no compressor/bag receipts or AVS scan data provided.

Single underside photo shows dry frame rail, driveshaft and exhaust with light surface patina only, no scaling, flaking or perforation — consistent with a car California-registered since new. Coverage is one view; rear frame section and hitch area not shown.

No engine-running instrument-cluster image or OBD scan in the material examined here. Seller says the truck 'runs and drives exceptionally well' but that is not a diagnostic test, and the AVS/height-control light is a known GX failure indicator.

Michelin Defender LTX M/S 2 stated on all four wheels; photos show an identical tread pattern front and rear with healthy depth. Date codes are not established, so age (not fitment) remains the open question.

No leaks disclosed and the engine bay photo appears clean and dry, but there is no radiator replacement record; the original plastic-tank radiator is the known GX failure point and the water pump job in March 2026 is not stated to have included it. No cold-start video or underbody-dry confirmation examined here.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: full VIN, Monroney label posted, itemised equipment, named dealer with $0 additional charges, no-reserve terms, free Carfax with 1-owner and 5 service records, and paint-meter readings published for the disclosed 2012 damage. Maintenance evidence is the weaker half: the timing belt/water pump, dashboard replacement and oil-service history are described and a shop is named, but no invoice images are reproduced in the text examined here, and there are no repair documents for the 2012 damage.

condition.rationale: 90k miles on a 20-year-old 2UZ-FE with a fresh belt and pump, an OEM replacement dashboard, a 2025 battery, matching Michelins, and paint/interior that photograph very well. Underside looks dry and unmolested. Pulling it down: a reported June 2012 damage event with no repair detail, an unknown radiator, unknown AVS/air-bag health, and no cluster or scan evidence. Low mileage does not substitute for the 20-year-old rubber, plastics and driveline fluids.

price_value.rationale: At the captured $15,888 bid this would be a bargain against comps (a 129k-mile 2008 sold for $24,000 on BaT; a 154k-mile 2006 brought $16,500), because 90k miles with Sport/KDSS and a fresh belt is the rare end of the market. But it is a no-reserve BaT auction with 444 watchers and five days left, and the realistic hammer plus BaT fee sits near the upper part of the buyer's price band, before the usual 20-year-old catch-up. Price discipline, not enthusiasm, has to set the bid cap.

mission_fit.rationale: This is the utility_capability branch done properly: body-on-frame V8, dual-range transfer case, Torsen center diff, KDSS articulation, receiver hitch, factory roof rack for a rooftop tent, third row and real dog/gear space — capability the unibody RX 350 does not supply. The overlap caution is real (it is a second big Lexus SUV), so it only earns its place if the off-pavement/tow/rack capability is genuinely wanted. It does nothing for the enthusiast manual brief and should not be counted against that list.

logistics.rationale: Belmont, CA is roughly a 90-mile drive from Carmel — an easy pre-bid inspection and an easy drive home, no transport needed. Toyota/Lexus mechanical is exactly what his mechanic recommends. California-registered since new, so smog and registration are routine. The only constraint is the auction clock: any PPI must be booked inside the five days before the 1:05 pm Pacific close on September 16.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Titanium Metallic over gray leather with the rarer dark Sport wood is a tasteful, unmodified, one-owner Bay Area truck with genuine character as a body-on-frame Land Cruiser Prado relative. It is an automatic SUV, however, and makes no claim on the manual enthusiast brief — the appeal here is competence and adventure utility, not driving reward.

positives: 90k miles on a one-owner, California-since-new GX470 with the timing belt and water pump stated done in March 2026 at ~86k — the single biggest GX price driver addressed.
Sport Package with KDSS, dual-range transfer case, Torsen center diff, receiver hitch and factory roof rack: real capability plus rooftop-tent mounting the RX 350 cannot offer.
Photos show a stock, level, unmodified truck with matching Michelin Defender LTX M/S 2 tires and a dry, patina-only underbody consistent with a lifelong California car.
OEM dashboard replaced with a receipt stated to exist, 2025 battery, ceramic coating applied — the common cracked-dash annoyance is already solved.
Cooperative dealer answering questions in detail, no reserve, $0 additional dealer charges, free Carfax and paint-meter readings published, and the car sits ~90 miles from Carmel.
concerns: Observed: Carfax reports damage in June 2012 and the seller published paint-meter readings, so refinish exists somewhere on the body; no repair invoices or severity detail are provided.
Observed: it is a no-reserve BaT auction with heavy watcher interest and five days left, so the final price is unknown and could land well above the current bid — a hard bid cap is required.
Unverified: the timing-belt/water-pump service is described and a shop is named but no dated invoice is shown (ask Willard's Auto Repair for the itemised receipt showing date, mileage and parts).
Unverified: rear height-control air bags, compressor and AVS status (request a video or PPI showing the truck raising and lowering through all heights and a scan for AVS/ABS codes).
Unverified: original plastic-tank radiator age — no replacement record; on a 20-year-old GX this is a known failure item (ask whether the radiator was replaced with the water pump).
Unverified: transfer case, front/rear differential and transmission fluid service history, plus tire date codes; a 90k-mile car can still be 20 years old on every fluid and rubber item.

Can you post an OBD-II scan report (all modules, including ABS/AVS) showing stored and pending codes?

Do you have records for transfer-case, front/rear differential and transmission fluid services, and at what mileages?
Has the rear air-suspension been serviced — any bag, compressor, height sensor or dryer replacement — and will you video the truck cycling through low/normal/high?
Can you photograph the rear frame rails, hitch mounting area and both lower ball-joint boots on a lift?
Is there a current California smog certificate, and will the sale include it?
ppi_focus: Verify the timing-belt job physically: inspect the belt covers/fasteners for recent service marks, check for coolant weep at the water pump and confirm thermostat/seal condition.
Radiator and cooling system: pressure test, inspect the plastic tank seams and transmission cooler for the known GX failure mode.
Rear air suspension: cycle all height settings, check bags for cracking, listen for a labouring compressor, and scan for AVS/height-control codes.
Lower ball joints (recall history) — check for play and boot integrity; also check upper control arm bushings and steering rack for weep.
Exhaust manifolds: listen at cold start for the classic 2UZ tick/crack.
Body repair survey: paint depth readings on every panel, panel gaps, seam sealer and inner-structure inspection to locate the 2012 damage repair.
Frame and underbody on a lift: rails, crossmembers, hitch mounts, rear shackle area — confirm the light patina seen in photos is the whole story.
Fluid condition and analysis: transmission, transfer case, front/rear diffs, brake fluid, coolant condition.
Full OBD scan of all modules plus a highway drive for transmission shift quality, KDSS behaviour and brake pulsation.
Tire DOT date codes and even wear pattern; confirm alignment and no tow-related rear-end abuse.
what_would_change_verdict: A photographed Willard's invoice showing the timing belt, water pump and related parts with date and mileage, plus a clean all-module scan, would move documentation and condition materially upward.
A body-shop record or a clean paint-meter/structural PPI showing the 2012 damage was cosmetic and properly repaired would remove the largest open risk.
Evidence of a sagging rear air suspension, an AVS/check-engine light, a weeping radiator or frame damage found at PPI would drop this well down the list.

A hammer price that pushes the all-in past the buyer's comfortable band for a 20-year-old truck that overlaps the RX 350 would turn a good buy into a poor one; disciplined bidding is the deciding variable.
evidence.mission_note: This satisfies the utility_capability brief on its own merits — body-on-frame V8, low-range, KDSS articulation, hitch, roof rack for a rooftop tent and third-row/dog space that the unibody RX 350 does not provide — and it is a Lexus, which is exactly what his mechanic endorses. It is not a bridge for the enthusiast manual brief; buy it only if the off-pavement and load capability itself is wanted alongside the RX, and bid to a fixed cap given the no-reserve format.
evidence.rationale: This is the strongest GX470 the tracker has seen in this branch: one California owner from new to 2026, 90k indicated miles, Sport Package with KDSS, stock presentation in every attached photo, and a dry, patina-only underbody that reads as a genuine West Coast truck. The two items that price a GX — timing belt and rear suspension — are partly answered: the belt and water pump are stated done in March 2026 at ~86k by a named San Jose shop, and the ride height is level with no lift or aftermarket parts visible, but neither is backed by an invoice or scan reproduced in the listing text. The OEM dashboard was replaced with a receipt said to exist, the battery is 2025, and the tires are matching Michelin Defender LTX M/S 2 with good depth, though date codes are unestablished. Against that, the Carfax shows a June 2012 damage entry and the seller has published paint-meter readings, which is commendable disclosure but not the same as repair documentation — the extent and quality of that work is the biggest open question. The radiator, transfer case, diff and transmission fluids have no records, which is the standard 20-year catch-up rather than a defect. Logistics are near-ideal: Belmont is a short drive from Carmel, PPI before the September 16 close is practical, smog is routine, and BaT shipping is unnecessary. The real risk here is price, not the car: comparable but higher-mileage examples sold from $10,251 to $24,000, and a no-reserve 90k-mile Sport with 444 watchers should be expected to finish near the top of that range. Set a cap, get the belt invoice and a lift inspection first, then bid.
